title: VerifySignatureResult
description: Result of `rebar verify-signature <ticket_id> --output json` (and the library verify_signature() / MCP verify_signature): a uniform verdict record. Every verdict carries the same base keys (manifest, step_count, algorithm, key_id, signed_at, head_sha) so consumers read them regardless of outcome; verdict is one of unsigned | foreign_key | certified | mismatch and verified is true iff certified. `foreign_key` no longer means "minted by another environment" (bug c21f: the signing environment is not a gate under current policy) — it now means no usable signer key could be obtained, or the opt-in `verify.require_environment` restriction is set and this cert is from a different environment. algorithm/key_id/signed_at/head_sha are null on an unsigned ticket. The not-found path emits an error_envelope instead (covered by ERROR_ENVELOPE).

signed_at.description: When the verified signature was created; null on an unsigned ticket. Nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC), from `time.time_ns()`. WIRE FORM: emitted as a JSON STRING of decimal digits ONLY — no sign, no thousands separators, no decimal point, no units suffix (e.g. "1787856371950409998") — whenever the value falls outside JavaScript's safe-integer range (|n| > Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 2**53-1 = 9007199254740991). That is a correctness measure for RFC 8259 §6 interoperability, NOT a formatting preference. CONSUMING IT: parse as an arbitrary-precision integer — `int(x)` in Python, `BigInt(x)` in JavaScript. Do NOT use `Number(x)`, and do not rely on a plain `JSON.parse` of the older numeric form: IEEE-754 binary64 rounds it SILENTLY, with no error — the real stored value 1787856371950409998 comes back from `JSON.parse` as 1787856371950410000. INVARIANT: the instant is unchanged and the conversion is lossless — the decimal digits are identical to the integer form; only the JSON type differs.

verdict.description: The verify-result verdict. `verified` is true iff `certified`. `key_not_valid_at_era` (epic gnu-whale-ichor) is the authorship-gate verdict for a cryptographically-valid signature by a key NOT valid at the event's commit. `invalid` / `unavailable` / `unknown_kind` / `unknown_scheme` (story 8d8e) are the op-cert dispatch verdicts: a malformed principal/namespace/envelope, a missing ssh-keygen, or a defensive registry miss. Display grouping: verified (certified) / unverified (mismatch | foreign_key | key_not_valid_at_era | invalid | unavailable | unknown_kind | unknown_scheme) / unsigned.

trust_basis.description: Which key certified an op-cert record (bug c21f): `own_key` = this environment's own op-cert key; `pinned_environment` = a key pinned out-of-band for the signing environment in .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml; `envelope_key` = the signer's own key as carried inside the SSHSIG blob — self-consistent (the signature, namespace and principal binding are all still checked in full) but not tied to a KNOWN environment. Null when no trust root was reached (an unsigned/legacy-HMAC record, or a refusal before key selection). The signing ENVIRONMENT is deliberately not a gate under current operator policy — `envelope_key` is an accepted basis — so this field exists to make the weaker basis VISIBLE rather than silently folded into `certified`. Restricting certification to a trusted set of environments is a future, opt-in feature (`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since`); when `verify.require_environment` is set, a cert from any other environment is `foreign_key` and the `envelope_key` basis is withheld.

rebar_version.description: The rebar gate code (version + short commit SHA, e.g. '0.6.0 (deadbee-dirty)') that produced the attestation — audit/provenance only, epic jira-reb-596. Null for pre-stamp or unsigned records.
